rewritten_reason: Read: (1) the two LastModified stamps: the copy objects were all written 2026-08-25T23:05:52Z; the originals now read 2026-09-02T00:15:12Z, 2026-09-02T00:15:18Z and 2026-09-02T00:15:23Z, all later. (2) The original bucket keeps versions: list-object-versions on the three exact keys shows 4 versions each, 3 of them written after the copy (2026-08-26 to 2026-09-02); the version that was current when the copy was taken has the copy's size AND the copy's ETag on all 3 days (ETags equal), so the copy is a faithful snapshot of the original as it stood on 2026-08-25 and the current original is a later write. The copy bucket holds 1 version per key. (3) The writer replaces a day object wholesale on a re-run: data/black_diamond/scripts/silver/merge-daily-incremental.py lines 183-190 (a re-landed bronze file changes the ETag, the per-date parquet is wholesale REPLACED), lines 196-207 and 545-546 (the ETag-keyed reprocess selection), lines 513-519 (to_parquet then _s3_upload to the same silver/transactions/<data date>.parquet key), and it drops transaction ids seen in the prior 30 days before writing (lines 474-507); it is run by the bronze-complete S3-event lambda (infra/aws/lambda/ci/lambda-source-map.json line 2385) and by SSM documents (infra/aws/ssm/opal-bd-transaction-download.json line 29, force-txn-download.json line 18). What the counts show: on 2026-08-22 and 2026-08-23 the original now holds 0 rows where the copy holds rows (4545 and 1035 distinct ids that the original no longer holds, 0 ids in common); on 2026-08-24 the reverse: the copy holds 0 rows and the original now holds 4864 rows over 1075 distinct ids that the copy lacks (0 in common). NOT_ESTABLISHED: which run wrote each later version and why the two earlier days now hold no rows (the 30-day id filter at lines 474-507 is one code path that can empty a re-written day, but no run log was read and the filter's effect on these days was not tested); whether the later versions of 2026-08-22 and 2026-08-23 hold rows (only the current version was read for rows; the earlier non-current versions were not read); what the rows of 2026-08-24 were before the copy (the version current at copy time has the copy's size, which is the empty-object size).
